sec-head.p: A standard AI model trained on text alone cannot interpret images, audio, or video, limiting its ability to understand real-world context. Multimodal AI solves this by fusing information from multiple modalities — text, image, and audio — enabling richer, more accurate responses without separate pipelines.

ul: Image captioning and visual question answering for accessibility tools
Video content analysis combining frames, speech, and metadata
Voice assistants with visual grounding for smart home and retail
Healthcare diagnostics merging medical imaging with clinical notes
Ecommerce product tagging from images, descriptions, and reviews
Cross-modal search retrieving results across text, images, and audio

faq-item.faq-a: Multimodal AI is an artificial intelligence architecture that processes and integrates data from multiple modalities — such as text, images, and audio — simultaneously. It enables richer understanding and generation by combining signals across different input types, rather than relying on a single modality.

faq-item.faq-q: How does multimodal AI differ from standard AI?
faq-item.faq-a: Standard AI models typically handle one modality (e.g., text-only LLMs). Multimodal AI fuses information from multiple modalities using dedicated encoders and alignment layers, allowing it to reason across formats like answering questions about an image or generating captions for a video.

faq-item.faq-q: What types of data can multimodal AI handle?
faq-item.faq-a: Multimodal AI can handle text, images, audio, and video, and often integrates structured data like tables or sensor readings. The exact modalities depend on the architecture, but common combinations include text+image, text+audio, and image+video+text.

faq-item.faq-q: How much does multimodal AI development cost?
faq-item.faq-a: A proof-of-concept starts at $2,000 to $5,000. A full production multimodal system ranges from $10,000 to $40,000 depending on modality count, data volume, and inference latency requirements. Contact for a fixed-price estimate specific to your use case.

faq-item.faq-q: How long does it take to build a multimodal system?
faq-item.faq-a: A proof-of-concept typically takes 3 to 5 weeks. A full production system with custom encoders, fusion logic, and deployment typically takes 6 to 12 weeks depending on data complexity and integration scope.
